subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Power of Breaks
description: A 60-second lesson on The Power of Breaks.

hook.text: A study of Israeli judges found parole approval dropped from 65% to near zero before lunch. Fatigue decided fates.

buildup.text: Your brain is not designed for sustained focus. After 90 minutes, performance degrades sharply.

discovery.text: Strategic breaks restore attention. A 10-minute walk outdoors boosts focus more than caffeine does.

twist.text: Scrolling your phone is not a break. It uses the same visual and cognitive circuits you are trying to rest.

climax.text: Work in 90-minute blocks with 15-minute true breaks. Move your body, rest your eyes, change your context.

punchline.text: Real breaks restore. Phone breaks drain further.

quiz.question: Why is scrolling your phone not an effective break?
options: It makes the break too long
It uses the same cognitive circuits you need to rest
It exposes you to negative news
